budget_affordability_frontier.note_free_budget: Agentic premium-at-risk cap $1,500 (HARD RULE 8) minus the SPY 2026-11-20 700P hedge at $749 cost basis. Settled cash $1,447.47 is NOT the binding constraint -- the budget cap is.
budget_affordability_frontier.conclusion: $751 buys AMD only at ~delta 0.15-0.18 and TSM only at ~delta 0.25 -- both below the ~0.35 default. The 0.35-delta strike costs ~$1,900 (AMD) / ~$1,100 (TSM). Liquidity and IV both PASS on these names (spreads 2-4% of mid, real OI, iv_rv ratios 0.68/0.77 = cheap); the ONLY blocker is the free budget.
budget_affordability_frontier.durable_rule_of_thumb: At 30-45 DTE a ~0.35-delta call costs roughly 0.045-0.065 x spot (IV 35-55%). With $751 free, the properly-sized universe is underlyings priced <= ~$130-150 at IV ~50%, or <= ~$200 at IV ~35%. Screening $400+ mega-caps against this budget is structurally futile -- future runs should either hunt in that affordable price band or accept the sleeve is hedge-dominated until the SPY hedge is closed/rolled (~21-DTE review 2026-10-30).
budget_affordability_frontier.anti_pattern_guard: Do NOT solve this by buying the cheap far-OTM strike that happens to fit. CLAUDE.md HARD RULE 8 names that exact trade-off as the failure the old $150 cap forced ('prefer the liquid, right-delta strike over a cheap illiquid one'). Sizing into the WEAKER of two setups because it is the one that fits the leftover budget is backwards -- flat is the correct position.

affordable_band_probe_2026_08_12_18Z.conclusion: CORRECTION to the 17:47Z 'structurally futile' framing. A ~0.35-delta INTC call costs $457.50 and a ~0.42-delta costs $595 -- both comfortably inside the $751 free budget, with OI of 10k-45k and spreads of 2-5% of mid. So the sleeve is NOT budget-locked into being hedge-only: at a ~$100 underlying the properly-sized, liquid, right-delta contract is affordable today. The binding constraint on THIS run was therefore setup quality (entry timing / trend-maturity), not money. That is a much better problem to have and future runs should stop re-deriving an affordability wall that only applies to the $400+ names.
